gloss: to microwave; to heat up in the microwave

definitions.gloss: to microwave; to heat up in the microwave
definitions.explanation: Casual, colloquial verb meaning to heat food in a microwave oven. Named after the 'chin' (ding) sound that microwaves make when finished.

examples.japanese: お{弁当|べんとう}をチンして。
{冷|つめ}たくなったら、チンすればいいよ。
examples.english: If it gets cold, just pop it in the microwave.

examples.japanese: {昨日|きのう}の{残|のこ}り{物|もの}をチンして、{夕飯|ゆうはん}にした。
examples.english: I microwaved yesterday's leftovers and had them for dinner.

notes:
An onomatopoeic する-verb derived from the チン sound (ding) that Japanese microwaves make when finished heating. Extremely common in casual speech — most Japanese people use チンする rather than the formal {電子|でんし}レンジで{温|あたた}める.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- チンして{食|た}べる: to microwave and eat
- チンするだけ: just microwave it (describing easy meals)
- レンジでチンする: to ding it in the microwave

USAGE:
Used in casual, everyday conversation. Not appropriate in formal writing. The word is understood by virtually all Japanese speakers regardless of age. Convenience store staff may ask: {温|あたた}めますか？ (Shall I heat it up?) — the formal equivalent of チンする.

RELATED WORDS:
- {電子|でんし}レンジ: microwave oven (the formal word for the appliance)
- {温|あたた}める: to heat up, to warm (the formal verb)
